title: Credo Brands Marketing Ltd - 544058 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Credo Brands (Mufti) Q1 FY27 revenue rose 5% YoY to INR125.3 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR26.6 crore (21.2% margin) as marketing and retail transformation spend rose.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 5% YoY to about INR125 crore, with gross margin at about 62% (61.6% per CFO). EBITDA fell to about INR27 crore from about INR31 crore a year earlier, mainly due to higher advertising, brand building and retail transformation spend. PAT was INR2.3 crore (1.8% margin). The company opened 5 stores and closed 7 underperformers, taking the count to 427. Management was cautious on near-term demand, which softened from mid-May, and declined to give growth projections for the next two years.

financial_highlights.change: down from about INR31 crore YoY
roughly INR5 crore higher YoY per analyst

segments.name: Retail (EBO stores)
segments.commentary: Store count at 427 after 5 openings and 7 closures in Q1; about 59% of stores are in Tier 2 and 3 cities. Average annual revenue per EBO was about INR75 lakh in FY26.

segments.name: D2C and digital
segments.commentary: Management said a growing share of marketing is going to Google and Meta, and the D2C business is being built, but no revenue figures were disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Marketing spend guided at 8% to 10% of revenue through FY27; Q1 was about 8.5%.
Same-store revenue growth targeted in the mid-single digits for FY27.
Management said it cannot give growth numbers for the next two years, and that Mufti 2.0 impact will be long drawn and may not show in the next few quarters.
Inventory days expected to decline modestly, per CFO, though CEO said inventory cycles are seasonal and inventory will not be larger.
No plans for a larger store count near term; focus is on productivity and brand consolidation rather than new markets.
capex_capacity: Store network at 427 after 5 openings and 7 closures in Q1 FY27; strategy is to replace low-productivity stores with experience-led stores on malls and high streets.
Stores are being renovated and retail identity refreshed; management cited early positive signals from renovated and new stores but declined to extrapolate.
Inventory is being sharpened through a merchandise mix change rather than a larger inventory base.
demand_pricing: Healthy consumer interest in April and part of May, which moderated from mid-May; management remains measured on near-term demand.
Discretionary spending remains soft, and competition is intense; some competitors spend 15% or more of revenue on advertising versus Mufti's 8% to 10%.
Pricing stays in the mid-premium segment; GP margin is reviewed each season and inflation cycle, with no change announced.
Management said all new stores are generating good revenue, but gave no figures.
No inventory write-offs in company history, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Are there early signs of improvement in discretionary consumption?
qa_highlights.answer: Positive signals from renovated and new stores and the new retail identity, but management said it is too early to extrapolate and would not give projections.

qa_highlights.question: Will the premiumisation strategy work across Tier 2 and 3 cities, where about 59% of stores are located?
qa_highlights.answer: Premiumisation is happening across India but is relative; each store is tailored to its local market and competitor set, not uniformly premium.

qa_highlights.question: Is the current investment for existing customer retention or new customer acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Both: retention of existing customers and acquisition of new footfall, especially among younger consumers.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue can the new premium-format stores reach at maturity, given FY26 average revenue per EBO of about INR75 lakh?
qa_highlights.answer: No maturity revenue figure given; the target is mid-single-digit same-store revenue growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Does premiumisation require more inventory and add working capital pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: No; inventory will not grow, and the change is to the merchandise mix only.

qa_highlights.question: Will revenue growth exceed the marketing spend increase within a year, given INR5 crore more revenue growth and INR5 crore more marketing spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not say that today. It said staying still is not right for the brand and that marketing is for long-term salience, not only performance marketing.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company in survival mode, and could it trade GP margin for growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management rejected the survival framing, said it is in a transformation phase, and said GP and pricing are reviewed each season, with the mid-premium positioning unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: When can growth return to pre-IPO trajectory, and what are inventory days expected to do?
qa_highlights.answer: No numeric timeline for growth beyond the next couple of years; CFO expects some reduction in the 74 inventory days, and CEO called inventory cyclical with no write-offs historically.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin compression: EBITDA fell about 13% YoY while marketing rose; watch whether the 8% to 10% marketing spend translates into footfall and revenue growth.
Demand softness: discretionary spending remained weak and demand moderated from mid-May, with no near-term visibility beyond one or two quarters.
Competitive intensity from brands spending 15% or more of revenue on advertising, plus Zara and other domestic and foreign brands.
Inventory days at 74 in Q1; the CFO expects some reduction, and the company has no write-offs to date.
Store closures and productivity: 7 closures in Q1 with a 427-store base; track same-store growth against the mid-single-digit target.
Management gave no multi-year growth guidance, which leaves visibility low.
summary.management_tone: Cautious and measured on demand, with confidence in the long-term brand thesis. Management avoided quantifying growth timelines and deflected questions on margin and store expansion, citing the transformation phase.
key_quotes: We are spending roughly 8% to 10%, and we intend to continue doing that.
We have not had any write-off in the history of our company on account of inventory.
it's going to be a longer drawn impact and not something that will be seen in a couple of quarters or 2, 3 quarters like that

adds.what: Net store reduction in Q1 FY27: 5 EBOs opened and 7 underperformers closed, taking count to 427

growth.why: Management guides only mid-single-digit same-store revenue growth for FY27 and 8-10% marketing spend, with no store-level numbers, timelines or orders behind it; it declined to give multi-year growth numbers and said demand softened from mid-May.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin fell to 21.2% (EBITDA about INR27 crore vs about INR31 crore YoY) as marketing runs at about 8.5% of revenue within an 8-10% FY27 guide, and management is in a transformation phase with no cost-action targets given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Store count fell net by 2 to 427 (5 opened, 7 closed in Q1), and management has no plans for a larger store count near term, focusing on replacing low-productivity stores instead.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides only mid-single-digit same-store revenue growth for FY27 against Q1 revenue growth of 5% YoY, with demand softening from mid-May and no store-level figures or orders behind it.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed and store network is being reshaped rather than expanded, with no utilisation figure disclosed to suggest a capacity need.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no multi-year growth numbers, cited softening demand from mid-May, and held guidance (mid-single-digit same-store growth, 8-10% marketing) without raising it.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA fell about 13% YoY and demand moderated from mid-May, while marketing is guided at 8-10% of revenue, so the margin and growth guide could slip if footfall does not respond.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or category launch was discussed; the focus is on merchandise mix and store renovation.

rows.label: Mufti 2.0 store renovation and retail identity refresh
rows.why: Management cited early positive signals from renovated and new stores but said Mufti 2.0 impact will be long drawn and may not show in the next few quarters, and gave no figures.

rows.label: Inventory days reduction from 74 days
rows.why: CFO expects a modest decline from 74 inventory days, but the CEO called inventory seasonal and cyclical, so the reduction is not firmly committed.

tone.note: Management was confident in the long-term brand thesis and renovated-store signals but cautious on demand after mid-May and declined to give multi-year growth numbers; analysts pushed on whether the INR5 crore extra marketing would produce matching revenue growth and on margin compression.
